newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-RANGERS WASTE CHANCES BUT STILL WIN 4-1.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RANGERS WASTE CHANCES BUT STILL WIN 4-1.

text.p: Glasgow Rangers missed a penalty and hit the crossbar twice but still cruised to a 4-1 victory over 10-man Hearts in the top Scottish premier league match on Saturday.
Rangers stay 14 points clear of Celtic, 1-0 winners at home to Dundee United. Celtic have three games in hand.
Rangers, chasing a record-equalling ninth consecutive league title, dominated the latest in a series of bad-tempered matches against Hearts.

England midfielder Paul Gascoigne hit the woodwork with a freekick after nine minutes before left-back David Robertson put Rangers ahead, surging through the Hearts defence from the halfway line before slotting the ball wide of former France goalkeeper Gilles Rousset.
Rangers captain Richard Gough had a header cleared off the line and team mate Alex Cleland hit the side-netting when clean through on goal as the visitors continued to threaten.
Then, on the stroke of halftime, Hearts had ex-Everton defender Neil Pointon sent off after his second clash inside a minute with Danish striker Erik Bo Andersen.

Pointon, one of four Hearts players sent off when the two sides met in a farcical league match at Ibrox in September, jumped for what appeared to be a 50-50 ball. Andersen fell to the ground like a lead weight and referee Bobby Tait reached for his red card.

Rangers took advantage of the extra man within minutes of the interval, Dane Brian Laudrup rounding Rousset to make the score 2-0 moments after Joerg Albertz had rattled the Hearts crossbar with a long-range strike.
And although veteran John Robertson pulled a goal back for Hearts, who at last showed signs of life, the champions never looked like letting the game slip.

Albertz restored their two-goal cushion from the penalty spot after Andersen had been dragged down in the box by Alan McManus, and then missed a second penalty after Gascoigne had been flattened as he headed for goal.
With six minutes left, Gascoigne capped the one-sided contest with a breakaway goal from a move started by Gough on the edge of his own penalty area.
"That's the best we've played for a few seasons here," Rangers boss Walter Smith said afterwards. "I'm pleased to get a result like that on what is always a very difficult ground."
Jim Jefferies, whose side have now lost three consecutive matches for the first time since he took over as manager at Tynecastle, blamed Hearts' lacklustre performance on injuries.
"We needed the strongest possible team playing as well as possible and we didn't have that today," he said. "If you look at what we were left with on the park it was men against boys really."

Hearts - 1-Gilles Rousset, 2-David Weir (12-John Colquhoun 88), 3-Neil Pointon (sent off 45), 4-Gary Mackay, 5-Alan McManus, 6-Paul Ritchie, 7-Stephane Phaille, 8-Steve Fulton (15- Grant Murray 70), 9-John Robertson, 10-Colin Cameron, 11-Neil McCann (14-Jim Hamilton 79)

Rangers - 1-Andy Goram, 2-Alex Cleland, 3-David Robertson, 4-Richard Gough, 5-Alan McClaren, 6-Ian Ferguson, 7-Trevor Steven (14-Ally McCoist 88), 8-Paul Gascoigne, 9-Erik Bo Andersen, 10-Joerg Albertz (16-Derek McInness 89), 11-Brian Laudrup.
